comment: The eight mutations the brief requires, each recorded as a CONCRETE PATCH — a file, an
anchor that must occur exactly once, and its replacement — never as a sentence describing
an edit. scripts/mutate.mjs applies and judges them.
A kill counts only when all four rules hold, and the script enforces all four: the owning
test PASSED unmutated in the same run; the patch actually CHANGED the file; the run served
the MUTATED code (the built bundle's hash must move, and the failure must not match a shape
that means the code never ran); and the failure is the owning assertion rather than the
suite going red. A patch that does not compile is DOES NOT BUILD and is never a kill.
Three kinds of owner, because this lab's evidence lives in three places:
kills      a rendered marker, naming the browser TEST and the exact CLAIM that kills it.
e2e/global-teardown.ts requires each of these to have been OBSERVED executing:
expectVerdict/expectClaim record every (test, marker, claim) they run, and the
rule is checked against that record rather than against the spec's source text,
because a mention is not an assertion.
specKills  a browser test that asserts something other than a marker (an arithmetic
re-derivation, for instance).
unitKills  a Vitest test, matched on its title.
The results of the last run are NOT written back here. e2e/global-teardown.ts already fails
the suite when a recorded kill never executed, so an archived 'observed' string would be a
second copy of an answer the suite already enforces. What the run produces is a ledger on
stdout; what guards the claim is the enforcement.

words-read-big-endian.why: Reads each 16-bit word big-endian. Folly reads little-endian, so the deployed digest must stop matching the reference checksum and the browser's SHA-256 must stop agreeing about the bytes.

folly-vector.test: folly-vector reports the comparison against the reference checksum

addition-drops-the-modulus-mask.find: for (let i = 0; i < p.N; i++) out[i] = reduceWord(a[i] + b[i], p.d);
addition-drops-the-modulus-mask.replace: for (let i = 0; i < p.N; i++) out[i] = a[i] + b[i];
addition-drops-the-modulus-mask.why: Adds without reducing modulo 2^d. The digest is then not an element of the group the hash is defined over, and words grow past the modulus the page says it is working in.
specKills: the headline claim: the digest after an add is the digest before plus the item vector, recomputed here
unitKills: every word stays below 2^d after addition and subtraction

remove-adds-instead-of-subtracting.replace: this.running = addWords(this.params, this.running, h); // mutated: remove adds
remove-adds-instead-of-subtracting.why: Implements removal as another addition. The four-step reference sequence removes "b", so the deployed digest must stop matching the Folly checksum, and the round-trip card — which drives the same add and remove on a live state — must stop reporting that the digest came back. The sibling verdict folly-removal-undone is deliberately NOT named here: it hashes the two items that remain from scratch, with no removal in it at all, and a mutation to removal has no business changing it.

remove-undoes-add.test: remove-undoes-add compares the digest before and after a round trip

folly-vector.test: folly-vector reports the comparison against the reference checksum

unitKills: add then remove returns to the original digest

blake2xb-node-offset-fixed-at-zero.why: Fixes the BLAKE2Xb node offset at 0, so every one of the 32 output blocks is a copy of the first. The expansion stops being an extendable-output function and the reference vector, which exercises all 32 blocks, must stop matching.

folly-sha256.test: folly-sha256 reports what the browser SHA-256 said about those bytes

unitKills: every output block differs from every other

recursion-stops-one-level-early.why: Calls the recursion finished with one modulus bit still uncancelled. The surviving vector is then only even, not zero, so the independent checker must refuse to call the result a collision.

collision-zero.test: collision-zero is the independent checker, not the recursion, reporting the zero

contains: same digest as the empty set

elimination-skips-the-row-swap.why: Never swaps the pivot row into place, so the elimination proceeds with a zero in the pivot position and the vector it reads out is not in the kernel. The checked read-out refuses it rather than handing the recursion a vector it would then halve.
unitKills: the kernel vector is in the kernel even when the pivot is not in the first row

verifier-compares-only-the-first-word.why: Stops the independent comparison after one word, so two digests that happen to agree in word 0 are reported as a collision. The page states how many words it compared, and that number must move.

verify-words-compared.test: the colliding set sizes sum to the number of items the checker re-hashed

unitKills: rejects digests that agree in the first word but differ later

query-counter-ignores-a-repeated-item.why: Counts only the first query for each item, hiding repeats behind a cache. The counter answers 'how many times did this page call the hash', and an item asked about twice is two calls.

update-queries.test: the query count claimed counts every call, including a repeat

unitKills: two queries of the same item are two queries and one distinct item
